question: Should the on/off state be a new mode of the existing ZestButton (the same button that stays pressed when it is on, like a Bold button in an editor), or a separate switch-style control (a sliding track and knob, like a settings switch)?
How should the button show that it is ON, so nobody has to guess? For example, a Bold button in an editor looks pressed in; you could also add a small tick or dot.
answer:
Pressed look plus a small check mark when on (recommended): On reads clearly even for people who cannot tell the
colours apart; the check animates in and out and is hidden from screen readers, which hear 'pressed' instead.
  Pressed look only (filled/tinted background, inset): Cleanest and smallest; relies on colour and shading alone to
tell on from off. And probably have the check mark position configurable to either start or end of button so we can still support icons too

question:
ZestButton gets an optional toggle mode, like a Bold button in an editor: it stays pressed when on and returns to normal when off. When on it shows a pressed look plus a small animated check mark; the check mark can sit at the start or end of the button so icons still work. Screen readers hear 'pressed' instead of the check mark. It is additive: buttons that do not turn it on look and behave exactly as before. It is for developers who install the library and for the people who use their apps.

What will be built:

1. R1: A developer can turn a ZestButton into a toggle through a new optional `zest.toggleOptions` prop. Without it the button renders and behaves exactly as it does…

2. R2: The on/off value can be controlled by the app (`pressed` plus `onPressedChange`) or left to the button (`defaultPressed`, off when not given). Each click or ke…

3. R3: When on, the button shows a pressed look (tinted or filled background with inset shading) plus a small check mark that animates in; when off, it shows the norm…

4. R4: The developer can choose whether the check mark sits at the start or the end of the button with `toggleOptions.checkPosition` ('start' or 'end'). Existing icon…

5. R5: The toggle is fully operable by keyboard and assistive technology: it is focusable, Space and Enter toggle it, it shows a visible focus ring in both states, an…

6. R6: The toggle looks right in light, dark and system themes, using the same theme variables as the rest of the button, and sizes everything in rem (px only for bor…

7. R7: A toggle works together with the existing button features: while disabled or busy it does not flip and shows its current state; with a confirmation it flips on…

8. R8: Toggle mode is documented where readers look: a first working example in README.md, recipes, the feature description, the new props and the 'additive, not brea…

9. R9: Tests prove that existing ZestButton behaviour is unchanged and that every toggle requirement above holds.

Assumed for you (tell me if any is wrong):

1. The toggle is additive: it is off unless the developer passes zest.toggleOptions, so existing buttons are unchanged.
2. Both app-controlled (pressed) and self-managed (defaultPressed) use are supported; pressed wins if both are given.
3. The check mark defaults to the start of the button when checkPosition is not given.
4. If onClick fails, the toggle keeps its flipped value; apps that need otherwise control `pressed`.

Not included:

• A separate switch control with a sliding track and knob
• Grouping toggles into radio-like or exclusive toggle groups
• Custom on and off icons other than the check mark (developers can still use iconLeft and iconRight)
• Remembering the on/off value between page loads

Are these right? Approve them, or tell me in your own words what to change.
optionLabel: Looks right, start designing, and write the documentation
